LESSON: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.2: Listening for Information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening for Information, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why should we listen attentively?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. paraphrase key ideas from an oral text for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the roles of extended family members.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information,

   Listening for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. paraphrase key ideas from an oral text for information,

   Listening for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the roles of extended family members.

   Listening for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an audio recording based on the family,

2. work with peers to pick out names of nuclear and extended family members from the recording,

3. team up to paraphrase key ideas on nuclear and extended family members from an oral text,

4. role-play the various members of the nuclear and extended family with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an audio recording based on the family,
2. work with peers to pick out names of nuclear and extended family members from the recording,
3. team up to paraphrase key ideas on nuclear and extended family members from an oral text,
4. role-play the various members of the nuclear and extended family with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening for Information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner engages actively with peers to paraphrase key ideas on

extended family members from an oral text.

• Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner shows personal presentation skills when roleplaying the various members of

the extended family with peers.

4

Values:
Integrity: This is developed as a learner displays transparency while answering simple questions about family members.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Gender appreciation: This is addressed as learners demonstrate harmonious coexistence with the other gender both in school

and at home.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate this concept about family to similar concepts covered in Social Studies.
